title: 816x624 or 1280 x720 Resolution in Rpg Maker Games

posts.author: Darkmoon9
posts.body:
Hi, I am kinda unsure if I should switch to 1280 resolution as some of my plugins work better that way. But I am not sure which
resolution is prefered overall. Do you think RPG Maker Assets scale well in 1280x720 resolution? Because I am not convinced everything works out, a few things look too small. On the other hand, seems like I do avoid the issue of having text clipping with
higher resolution.
What resolution does most people on this forum use, 816x624 or 1280x720 or neither (Perhaps even higher.)

posts.author: bgillisp
posts.body:
720 is a height of 15 tiles if you use default tiles. Many games in older engines used resolutions with 15 tiles for height and worked out well. So I'd suggest at minimum 960 x 720 (which is also 20 tiles wide, 15 tiles high).
That gives it an old school 4:3 look though, so have to decide if that is what you want.
If you go higher I'd suggest considering a zoom plugin too as you will have maps showing too much the higher the resolution goes.

posts.author: Nirriti
posts.body:
Smaller res forces a nice natural zoom and cuts off 'empty dead space' on the screen. At the same time, itll cause issues with font
(which will require you to use sharpening plugins).
Spoiler:
Font Troubles Insanity
If said font has slightly blurry edges—which was the case for mine—it might require you to split the entire font into 2 PNGs (one for outlines) and edit both by hand. If you added a boatload of characters, youll also multiply the amount of work by a lot... Going down that route has a nice side effect... The font file itself only tells the game what keyboard characters your game can "read" and use (add to that via FontForge). So... the two PNGs youve made for said font are the ACTUAL graphic files used for the letters/numbers/special char. in your game. What this means is you can easily edit all of it manually. Hakuhen's plugin(s) sent me into a pretty deep rabbithole which ate DAYS. But you know what? Now its all perfect (or close enough as sometimes I was forced to "break alignment"). Was able to fix my font by the pixel. Remade my V(s) and Y(s) to my taste. Its not hard, its just incredibly time consuming to do every slot by hand, one by one (let alone placing them all in line).
If you look at the "J" its slightly blurry. Well the smaller res game, being stretched to fullscreen, caused many characters to look downright gross (like the "/" sign). Its not as bad for bold characters, as you can see here, but thinner parts really were beyond the pale "ugh" looking, in-game. Went off a pretty weird tangent. You probably wont need to do all that. Just explaining some pros and cons from my limited experience. EDIT: Fixed the "A".
USER INTERFACE
: Theres plugins to adjust everything. I highly recommend
@Aerosys
's plugins. Easy to use and test in real time. No BS obfuscation, no coding required. If you go towards a naturally smaller res, its just a must. Also helps to add elements and fix some misalignment problems too.
